anchors.text: A randomized trial assigns eligible consenting participants to interventions by chance. Concealing the next assignment protects enrolment against foreknowledge; blinding concerns awareness after assignment. These are different design features. Randomization reduces treatment-selection confounding but leaves possible chance imbalance, missing outcomes and limits on applicability. The comparator, endpoint, analysis and conduct determine what the comparison establishes.

anchors.text: Clinical-trial phases describe development purposes rather than a fixed sample size, assignment method or promise of benefit. Phase 1 studies administration, exposure, safety and dosage, sometimes with early activity measures. Phase 2 asks whether activity and safety support further study in a specified population. Phase 3 compares with a defined alternative and can provide evidence for an approval decision; a phase 3 label is not itself approval. FDA's patient overview illustrates phase 3 with hundreds to thousands of participants, while the actual size follows the protocol's question and information requirements. Phase 4 studies an approved treatment in broader use. Read the protocol because phases can overlap or be combined.

anchors.text: Publication format and review status describe what can be inspected and what scrutiny a report has received. A conference abstract, preprint, full article and correction can report different versions of one study. Identify the study and version, read the available methods and match every result to its population, endpoint and data cutoff. Peer review adds scrutiny; it does not establish that every conclusion is correct or independently replicated.

anchors.text: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) uses antibody binding and signal development to show a selected protein in a prepared tissue section. Interpretation retains which cells and compartments stain, the intensity and distribution, and the named marker-specific method. A percentage, intensity category or composite score can describe different aspects of the result. Fixation, retrieval, controls, sampling and observer variation affect interpretation. Automated quantification also needs validation for its marker, specimens and intended use. A research stain or generic score does not replace a validated clinical selection assay.

anchors.text:
Immune-related adverse events are injuries attributed to treatment-related immune activity, commonly discussed with checkpoint inhibitors. They can affect the bowel, lung, skin, liver, hormone-producing glands and other organs. A symptom or laboratory change during treatment does not by itself establish an immune cause.

Clinical assessment identifies the organ, severity, timing and competing explanations. Reactions can arise after treatment stops, and some endocrine injury leaves lasting loss of function. Organ-specific management can include different measures, such as treatment interruption, immunosuppression or hormone replacement. An adverse event, an attributed immune injury and a cancer-response result are separate findings.

anchors.text: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

anchors.text: RNA carries cellular messages; bulk sequencing samples those messages from combined tissue after protocol-specific capture and preparation. Analysis assigns usable observations to genes or transcripts and applies a defined comparison scale. A change can reflect cell composition, expression within cells or both. Gene totals can conceal transcript differences, and pooled RNA does not directly establish protein localisation, pathway flux or drug dependence.

anchors.text:
Immuno-PET uses radiolabelled antibodies or antibody-derived binders. Full immunoglobulin G (IgG), antigen-binding fragments (Fab), minibodies and single-domain nanobodies differ in size and pharmacokinetics. The format can affect penetration, clearance, retention and normal-organ background; there is no universal best format. A label makes the binder traceable, not a perfect detector of every target site.

The radionuclide must suit the product's imaging time course. Dijkers' 89Zr-trastuzumab study examined a full antibody over several days; Keyaerts' 68Ga-HER2 nanobody study imaged at earlier times. These are product-specific examples. Antibody imaging can concern a tumour-associated target or immune cells. CD8 binder imaging belongs here; granzyme-B peptide or peptidomimetic imaging is a different tracer class and has its own record.

anchors.text: Calibrated activity measurements, often from suitable serial SPECT or PET imaging, inform a time-activity model. Time-integrated decays, emission properties, tissue mass and spatial assumptions then inform absorbed dose. Equal uptake on an early scan can be followed by different retention and different doses. Administered activity is an input, not a substitute for patient- or tissue-level dosimetry. The estimates can support evaluation of dosing strategies, but improved outcomes from a particular adaptation require their own evidence.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Lutetium-177 therapies deliver beta-particle radiation through target-binding molecules. VISION tested PSMA-targeted treatment added to protocol-permitted standard care in selected, previously treated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. NETTER-1 tested lutetium-177-dotatate in progressive, somatostatin-receptor-positive midgut neuroendocrine tumors. Their clinical results belong to those populations and products, rather than every tumor expressing the target. Small molecules, peptides and antibodies have different distribution and clearance even when directed at a shared target.

anchors.text:
Radiation transfers energy to tissue and can damage DNA directly or through reactive molecules. Cells can repair damage or lose their ability to keep dividing, and death can occur later. One treatment session is an exposure, rather than an immediate count of dead cells. Oxygen, cell state and repair affect the response.

External beams, brachytherapy sources and systemically distributed radiopharmaceuticals have different exposure patterns. An external-beam target can include tissue at risk of microscopic disease after surgery, even when no mass is visible. Planning and verification consider geometry, motion, normal organs and previous overlapping exposure. Precision does not eliminate normal-tissue dose or injury.

Absorbed dose in gray is energy per mass: one gray is one joule per kilogram. Total dose, fraction size, timing and exposed volume influence biological effects. Physical-dose arithmetic alone does not establish equivalence of schedules. Local or regional control, symptom relief, distant disease and survival remain distinct clinical outcomes.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text:
Stereotactic body radiotherapy, also called SABR, uses specialised localisation, planning, positioning, image guidance and delivery to give a high dose per fraction to a body target outside the brain. A small number of visits does not establish that this delivery package was used. A biologically effective dose calculation compares modelled effects under assumptions; it does not document stereotactic localisation, motion management or verification. Modern non-stereotactic radiotherapy can also use imaging, conformal beams and motion assessment.

The target, motion, dose distribution, positioning uncertainty, prior overlapping radiation and normal-organ constraints determine the coverage problem. Dose falls through space rather than stopping at a drawn line. There is no universal one-centimetre safe boundary, lesion-size ceiling or prescription that applies to every organ. Planned exposure, verified delivery, local control and toxicity need their own measurements.

A 2010 prospective study concerned medically inoperable peripheral early-stage lung cancer and measured local control, distant failure and toxicity. That setting does not validate treatment of every central lesion or organ. CURB and NRG-BR002 tested different metastatic settings and comparisons. Local control, added progression-free or overall survival, symptom relief and an immune response are separate outcomes.

anchors.text:
Freezing and thawing can injure cells through ice formation, osmotic changes and vascular injury. The historical mechanistic literature emphasises temperature, time, thawing and repetition; a probe setpoint is not exposure everywhere in the tissue. The visible frozen region and the lethal boundary need separate assessment.

Georgiades and colleagues studied normal renal tissue in swine. Measurements from six test animals found a mean nonlethal rim of 0.75 millimetres, with variation and widening near large vessels. Their proposed six-millimetre visible-ice margin for renal cancer was an extrapolation under stated assumptions, rather than a measured universal human margin.

Site, geometry, applicators and nearby structures affect feasibility and harm. Freezing, preserved material or local tissue destruction alone does not establish antigen presentation, useful immune priming or distant tumour control.

anchors.text: A case report documents a clinical course, interventions, outcomes and alternative explanations. It can reveal a signal of benefit or harm without establishing what would have happened under another approach. The CARE reporting guideline includes a timeline, diagnostic assessment, interventions, follow-up, the patient perspective and consent; complete reporting supports appraisal rather than proving treatment causation.

anchors.text: Preclinical and nonclinical work studies mechanisms, activity, exposure and safety using specified models. Such experiments can occur before or alongside human studies. Evidence that a model responds does not establish a useful treatment for patients. FDA nonclinical requirements depend on the product and context; its published approaches include justified reductions or replacements of animal studies, so a universal two-species requirement is inaccurate.

anchors.text: A comparison between separate studies must account for differences in participants, treatment, background care, endpoints, clocks and follow-up. Randomisation protects the comparison within a trial; it does not randomise participants between unrelated trials. Formal indirect comparisons can retain within-trial contrasts through a common comparator, but depend on compatible effect modifiers and methods. A higher headline percentage in one study is insufficient to rank treatments.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: In a local-treatment study, follow injury and signals through presentation, priming, recognition and measured tumour outcomes. Circulating cytokines or proliferating T cells alone do not establish tumour-specific killing, distant control or an optimal radiation dose.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Compare later challenge with living matched tumour cells in vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts, and test specificity with unrelated compatible tumour cells. Incidence and growth are functional readouts. Immune-competent versus deficient comparisons alone cannot isolate immunogenic death from other immunostimulation. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Residual inducer, contamination, incompatible antigens and poor death confirmation can invalidate attribution. No universal DAMP cutoff establishes immunogenicity.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Death plus extracellular ATP does not establish a cancer vaccine. Danger signals, cross-priming, functional protection, distant control and patient benefit are separate claims. Even a positive mouse vaccination assay remains model-bound and does not select a clinical treatment.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: The strategy uses relevant tumour antigens in place while supporting presenting cells and immune activation. Antigen availability, uptake and processing, cross-presentation, suitable priming, access to another lesion, recognition of naturally displayed targets and useful function are conditional jobs. Local injury can supply material without establishing all these steps, and danger signals alone do not establish immunogenic cell death. An uninjected lesion can still be exposed to systemic drugs.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Assessment combines local sampling, controlled immune assays and serial treated/uninjected-lesion measurements. Tissue, blood and viable cells are finite inputs. Keep local change, specified reactive-cell counts or functions, and response proportions under their stated rules separate. No universal marker proves successful vaccination. Nonspecific inflammation, added peptide, viability, missed sampling times and concurrent therapy can confound results; a model or assay needs separate clinical validation of the complete intervention.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Added peptide can bypass natural processing. Appropriate naturally presenting targets and recognition or cytotoxicity controls address a separate bridge, within the model’s limits. In a fictional study, the injected lesion shrinks and blood cells respond to supplied tumour peptides, while another lesion is unchanged. Local activity and assay reactivity were observed; natural recognition, access and useful distant function remain unproven. The unchanged lesion also does not establish absence of every immune-learning event.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: For T-cell-directed therapeutic strategies, compare the antigen source and what can be selected beforehand. An in-situ approach uses tumour material in the body and selects a site and intervention; a supplied design selects planned composition or encoded targets using adequate sample information or material. Defined peptide or encoded targets differ from broader cell preparations. Manufacturing a product does not mean every peptide ultimately displayed is known or controlled. The room-material versus teaching-kit analogy describes these inputs, not assured learning or a winner.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Priming is initial activation of a naive T cell. Cross-presentation places externally acquired material on class I HLA in a presenting cell; that event is distinct from a cancer cell naturally displaying a recognised target. Both strategies still need evidence of presentation, suitable priming or expansion, tumour access, useful function, outcomes and harms. Dashed links in a comparison diagram mark questions to investigate, not successful completion of each step.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: The required opportunity depends on the method. A lesion-based local approach needs available tumour material at an identified, safely accessible site. A supplied product needs appropriate information or material and a workable manufacturing and delivery plan. If no identifiable lesion is accessible, that removes the stated opportunity for that local method; it does not show that another vaccine is feasible or choose treatment. Match a research question about local material and support to that design, or one about planned antigen selection to a supplied design, then compare complete strategies in suitable studies.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: An interpretable tracer record retains the exact binder and format, isotope, protein mass in micrograms or mg, administered activity in MBq and time after injection. Background in blood and normal organs, lesion size and clearance affect interpretation. One image cannot isolate every delivery, binding and retention contribution, quantify receptor occupancy or supply a therapeutic absorbed dose. Protein mass is not a target-positive cell fraction, and uptake is not an expression percentage.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Absorbed dose in gray (Gy) is energy deposited per tissue mass, with 1 Gy equal to 1 joule per kilogram. Administered activity in MBq measures radioactive decays per time, not energy absorbed. A single uptake image or SUV is neither quantity. Dose estimation needs an appropriate time-activity model, emissions and energy-deposition assumptions for the relevant tissue. Equal early uptake can precede different retention. The tested diagnostic tracer cannot supply a different therapeutic product's dose merely because both bind the same target.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Radioactive activity is a decay rate in becquerels; absorbed dose is deposited energy per mass in gray. A single bright image is not time-integrated exposure. Dosimetry combines suitable activity measurements or models over time with tissue geometry and emission properties. Neither the targeting-molecule mass nor the administered activity alone specifies tumor dose.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Radioimmunotherapy uses an antibody carrier. The broader radiopharmaceutical category also includes organ-seeking products without a separate targeting ligand. Not every attachment uses a metal chelator. Alpha and beta emissions have different path and energy-deposition properties; neither label alone ranks safety or effectiveness. Daughter redistribution and microscopic geometry can matter.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Radiation can deposit energy beyond the cell carrying the radioactive product, so chemical-payload uptake into each neighbouring cell is not the same requirement. Binding and internalisation can affect retention, but the complete carrier's distribution, biological removal, radionuclide decay and tissue geometry still determine delivery. A diagnostic tracer image is not a measured therapeutic absorbed dose, and resistance to a chemotherapy payload does not itself establish radiation sensitivity or safe organ exposure.
anchors.sourceScope: Current field re-read and semantically compared. Retains inherited source assessment and its depth; no claim that every sentence in this field was freshly primary-verified.

anchors.text: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is made up of DNA fragments shed by tumour cells into the bloodstream

anchors.text: A product proposal identifies the clinical problem, disease setting, treatment intent, alternatives and measurable goal; the exact target, specimen and method; accessible protein or peptide-HLA presentation and normal-tissue evidence with sampling limits; and the complete binder, linker, payload or cell design and mechanism. It records the relevant human comparison or explicitly limited preclinical evidence, product-specific safety monitoring, management capability and stopping rules. Keep manufacture, quality release, sponsor, site and access pathway separate from benefit. Reviewing existing data, consuming tissue for an experiment, manufacturing and administering treatment are different commitments with their own rationale and responsible owner. A target shortlist or recipe analogy establishes none of their benefit or safety.
anchors.sourceScope: Unchanged registered teaching reread in full. The listed abstracts and targeted regulator sections were read here; Morgan full text remains inaccessible. Context and fictional premises are retained, not upgraded to treatment evidence.

anchors.text: Questions follow the product. For a cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugate, assess antibody, linker and payload together, delivery and exposure, tested resistance steps and the design-specific role of internalisation; FDA's March 2024 clinical-pharmacology guidance has this scope. For an engager or cell product, ask about cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity and other neurologic effects, healthy-tissue recognition, tissue access and what can persist after dosing stops. FDA's January 2024 CAR T-cell guidance describes product-specific recognition, expansion, persistence and toxicity management; it does not supply incidence for every engager. For a radioligand, ask how the imaging relates to that therapeutic product's distribution, organ absorbed doses and organ limits. FDA's August 2019 document addresses nonclinical studies and labeling, not a universal clinical dose threshold. Tracer uptake supplies no CAR-T safety threshold. For a T-cell-receptor proposal, ask which peptide-HLA target is recognised and how specificity, natural presentation and function were tested; receptor sequences or expanded clones alone leave these questions open.
anchors.sourceScope: Unchanged registered teaching reread in full. The listed abstracts and targeted regulator sections were read here; Morgan full text remains inaccessible. Context and fictional premises are retained, not upgraded to treatment evidence.

anchors.text: Product Q is a fictional investigational conjugate against surface protein M, with a specified antibody, cleavable linker and cell-damaging payload. Adults with progressing metastatic solid cancer after prior treatment are the setting, and the immediate proposal is to review existing data before designing a laboratory experiment. No manufacture, treatment or new sample collection is proposed. The dossier has M RNA measurements from one tumour biopsy and Q activity in target-bearing cultured cells, without direct surface measurement, relevant healthy-tissue tests or a human comparison. Supplier participation, access and site arrangements are unknown. These findings support a research hypothesis about Q, not demonstrated clinical benefit or evidence borrowed from another M-targeted format.
anchors.sourceScope: Unchanged registered teaching reread in full. The listed abstracts and targeted regulator sections were read here; Morgan full text remains inaccessible. Context and fictional premises are retained, not upgraded to treatment evidence.

anchors.text: Complete the fictional Q card by retaining accessible tumour protein, healthy-tissue effects, full-product delivery and relevant human outcomes as missing evidence. A research lead first reviews methods, controls and Q-specific product data; this existing-data review consumes no tissue. Pause experiment planning if product identity or usable evidence remains unavailable, and ask which Q-specific result would change the experiment plan. RNA abundance is a different observation from accessible surface protein. Mertins and colleagues measured RNA, protein and phosphoprotein layers in primary breast cancers; that work is not a cell-surface-accessibility or treatment-selection assay. Confirming protein would answer another premise while leaving benefit unproven.
anchors.sourceScope: Unchanged registered teaching reread in full. The listed abstracts and targeted regulator sections were read here; Morgan full text remains inaccessible. Context and fictional premises are retained, not upgraded to treatment evidence.

anchors.text: Now change only the fictional request: after complete tumour removal, someone proposes manufacturing Q and administering it to prevent recurrence because M RNA was abundant, an IND is said to be active and a supplier offers manufacture. The setting and commitments have changed, while the dossier is still one biopsy RNA signal plus cultured-cell activity. Neither that evidence nor the attributed investigational milestone or supply offer establishes postoperative benefit. Ask the clinical team for Q-specific human evidence or a relevant protocol, the sponsor which product and protocol are covered, and the readiness owner about delivery requirements. In the United States an effective Investigational New Drug application is not marketing approval, and submission of a Biologics License Application is not its approval. A manufacturing quote cannot confirm supply, consent, review, delivery and monitoring as a whole. With only this dossier, evidence and pathway review are justified; manufacture or administration is not justified by the supplied information. Speculative availability does not promise access or protection against recurrence.
anchors.sourceScope: Unchanged registered teaching reread in full. The listed abstracts and targeted regulator sections were read here; Morgan full text remains inaccessible. Context and fictional premises are retained, not upgraded to treatment evidence.

anchors.text: NCI biospecimen guidance places pathology oversight of tissue release alongside the need to protect complete medical evaluation. It also treats divided and extracted material as traceable derivative samples. A thoracic small-specimen guideline addresses triage and handling for multiple ancillary studies in its own clinical scope. The general resource issue is finite material, not a universal order of tests: remaining tissue and assay requirements need to be established for the actual specimen.
anchors.sourceScope: Current selected source passages and source-first reasoning at the recorded depth; no whole-document reading or independent acceptance.

anchors.text: Cutting sections moves material from the block onto slides; extraction consumes a portion and loses its original architecture. Stored images and datasets can be copied and reanalysed but cannot refill the archive. A newly collected biopsy is another procedure and time point, and a growing culture is a changed system rather than replenishment of the original specimen.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: An aliquot is an allocated portion. Retain site, date, treatment context, preservation, region, quantity, prior uses, remaining material, permissions and custody. A block list or ten remaining slides does not prove that relevant malignant cells remain. Returning a block does not replace extracted tissue.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: Fictional small block: one proposed extraction remains possible after diagnostic needs are protected, while two teams request overlapping RNA tests. Compare questions, validated inputs, existing-data reuse, permissions and expected material use with pathology before allocation. No universal section count, percentage budget or clinical priority follows from this exercise.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: Specimen allocation starts by identifying the available portions, assessing their suitability, estimating method-specific use and recording consumption. Blocks, slides, frozen pieces and cell aliquots are finite inputs; their counts alone do not establish adequacy. Record remaining portions with section thickness, area or analyte amounts and the relevant context. Receiving-laboratory requirements and diagnostic priorities apply, rather than a universal test budget. Outdated inventories, unrecognised exhaustion, unsuitable regions and duplicated destructive work can waste material. Specimen governance supports reliable testing but is not itself a clinical biomarker and does not establish whether a test changes care or another procedure is appropriate.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: Keep physical portions and their custody separate from reusable data. The record links collection site and time, treatment context, preparation, represented region and cells, prior use, remainder, holder and permitted use. Permission to analyse a dataset does not itself permit transferring or consuming its source block. For an authorised physical use, track the portion, sender, recipient, handling, receipt, consumption and remainder at each handoff. A returned block does not restore cut or extracted material. Diagnostic evaluation, patient safety and applicable consent take priority; the receiving laboratory and pathology must resolve actual suitability rather than infer it from quantity alone. Before allocation, specify the question, receiving method, minimum usable input, processing and transport timing, assay controls and what remains for other needs. These are method-specific requirements rather than a universal number of biopsy cores.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: In an invented archive, one FFPE block came from a breast lesion collected on teaching day zero after systemic treatment. The last pathology review identified a mixed region of tumour, scar and immune cells. Diagnostic sections were cut earlier, but usable depth and relevant remainder are unknown. Pathology holds the block and must establish its diagnostic reserve; permission covers named molecular and image projects but no physical transfer. Lab A accepts FFPE and requests four five-micrometre sections: hold cutting until pathology confirms suitable remainder and the laboratory confirms input and permissions. Lab B requires living tumour cells: reject this fixed block for that request and ask which compatible input would be needed, without authorising another collection. The image team may reuse the already permitted teaching image version one from the last reviewed slide level without new cutting, recording its version and source slide. This is a complete allocation decision despite a named hold, not a standard section count or reserve percentage.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: If pathology later confirms enough suitable remainder after its reserve, the fictional DNA request still needs laboratory input confirmation and the required permissions before use. Update cuts, custody and remainder when the authorised work occurs; the fixed block remains incompatible with the original-living-cell request. New blood collection is another timepoint with its own requirements, not replenishment of an old specimen. A large tumour bed can contain scar, normal tissue and immune cells, so total quantity cannot establish the needed cells or assay fit.
anchors.sourceScope: Unapplied PR-373 proposal. Selected NCI biospecimen sections read; fictional quantities, permissions and laboratory acceptance are assumptions, never standard input or allocation rules.

anchors.text: Paired-specimen studies found that fixation and extraction changed nucleic-acid measurements relative to fresh-frozen material. Viable organoid studies examine a different property: whether living cells can establish the studied culture. Preserved morphology, recoverable DNA or RNA, and viable cell behavior are therefore different specimen requirements. No preparation is universally best; the intended measurement and evidence for that particular workflow determine suitability.
anchors.sourceScope: Current selected source passages and source-first reasoning at the recorded depth; no whole-document reading or independent acceptance.

anchors.text: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded material preserves architecture and supports assays validated for its altered molecules, but cannot restore the original living cells. Snap-freezing preserves material for molecular analysis; the NCI protocol excludes viability, sorting and culture endpoints. A viable-cell vial requires verified recovery, identity and function for its intended assay. No preparation label measures tumour content.

anchors.text: Assess suitability by documenting preservation, checking which cells are represented and applying quality checks for the intended assay or living-cell workflow. Sections, tissue pieces and cell aliquots are finite, and destructive quality checks also use material. Report analyte-appropriate yield and quality, or viable-cell recovery and function when those are required. The receiving method defines acceptance: a preservation label alone guarantees no pass. Delayed stabilisation, incompatible fixative, degraded analyte, poor thaw recovery and missing target cells can defeat the question. Validation on fixed tissue does not automatically transfer to frozen or cultured material, and input suitability alone proves neither clinical accuracy, tumour-wide representation nor patient drug response.

anchors.text: Match the named request to the actual preparation. FFPE can support a validated fixed-tissue assay if the relevant region remains, but cannot supply the original living cells. Snap-frozen material needs a compatible method and handling history; molecular preservation does not establish viable recovery. Viably cryopreserved material needs a suitable recovery protocol and the relevant living cells checked. Fresh tissue needs the receiving laboratory's processing and transport requirements. Blood or leukapheresis may suit a specified immune-cell or comparison workflow but does not substitute for tumour; a plasma cfDNA or ctDNA assay has its own collection, handling and timepoint requirements.

anchors.text: Slyper's 2020 tumour toolbox used single-cell profiling for fresh material and single-nucleus profiling for frozen material, with tissue-specific customisation. Matched preparations typically recovered similar cell types but sometimes different proportions. Some frozen specimens can supply nuclei without recoverable living cells, and neither preparation label guarantees a useful dataset. A new collection cannot recreate the original specimen's place and time; a successful model or molecular assay does not establish clinical treatment benefit.
